a.text: Don't start. Please. Not tonight, Eli.

b.text: I'm not starting. I'm looking at your face. Your face is starting things.

c.text: It's nothing. A disagreement. About numbers.

e.text: ...Crowe's. Look, I had a system. The system had a bad week.

f.text: Boy, sit down before you fall down. Both of you eat something. Then we talk like family, not like debtors.

a.text: Four hundred by Friday and it stops growing. That's all I need. That's ALL.

give.text: You're— okay. Okay. I'll make it right, Eli. I swear on Ma.

refuse.text: Fine. FINE. Then I'll handle it like a man. ...Don't look at me like that, that's exactly what I'm doing.

a.text: Two men. Van with berth plates. Julian Crowe was walking beside them like he owned the alley. Because for tonight, he did.

c.text: Toward the water. They always go toward the water, child. That's where they keep their mistakes.

d.text: You want your brother back, you go see Silas in daylight. Crowe respects daylight. It's the only thing he fears.

a.text: Ledger? Crowe's book? Honey, that book has more bodyguards than the mayor.

b.text: I don't need the book. I need one page. Marcus's page.

c.text: Pages move. Julian tears them out to sell names he's finished with. I've seen three surface this month. I buy them quiet.

d.text: Bring me pages, I pay. Bring me twelve, I'll tell you who's been BUYING them. And that, sugar, is a different conspiracy.

a.text: Fifteen hundred by Friday. Options?

crew.text: Roz pays on delivery and never asks what's in the crate. That's either trust or a trap with good manners.

jobs.text: Legit. Slow. Clean hands, empty pockets by Sunday. Ma would've liked it.

shake.text: Julian's collectors carry envelopes and grudges. Take the envelopes. Make it loud enough that Crowe calls ME.

a.text: We're closed. And open. Depending on your business and its volume.

b.text: Marcus Vane's note. Who holds it now?

c.text: That's client information. That's— ...that's two hundred. And you didn't smell like cop when you came in, so I'll say it once.

d.text: Mr. Crowe sold the note last Tuesday. Bought it out from under him: a Halcyon subsidiary. 'Halcyon Civic Holdings'. Whatever your brother stole, son, it wasn't money.

a.text: Eli Vane. In my office. Either you're desperate or I'm dreaming, and I never dream about men with good jawlines.

c.text: There's a crate van. Berth seven to Yard four, twenty minutes, no stops. The crate is none of your business. That's the job AND the paycheck.

d.text: One more thing. If blue lights show, you decide who you are before they decide for you. Everyone out here learns that arithmetic eventually.

a.text: Sweep ahead! Two cruisers, checkpoint, the whole theatre! Talk fast, Vane!

dump.text: Crate goes in the channel. We go through empty and boring.

run.text: Hold on to something, Dex. Boring was never on the menu.

a.text: Sit. The chair by the window; the light flatters honest men. ...You're not flattered. Interesting.

c.text: Fifteen hundred, plus the courtesy of not having your collectors' ribs inventoried last night. I keep receipts, Mr. Vane. Of everything.

d.text: Understand me: I am not your enemy. I am your brother's arithmetic. Enemies are much warmer people.

pay.text: Counted twice, as is custom. The note is retired. Your brother, however, remains... in circulation.

time.text: A week. Seven sunrises. I'll mark it in the book in pencil, Mr. Vane. Pencil is the most expensive ink I own.

threaten.text: ...There. Now we're acquainted. Take your hand off my desk before I invoice you for it.

a.text: A courtesy, since you asked so rudely. I no longer hold your brother's paper. It was purchased. Above me, considerably above.

c.text: Halcyon Civic Holdings. Which means your brother didn't borrow from me. He borrowed from the people who are buying this city by the debt. I merely introduced them.

d.text: Find what he took from them, Mr. Vane, and you will never need me again. You'll have much worse creditors.

a.text: You still take your coffee like an insult, or did marriage fix that?

c.text: Semantics. Sit. I have thirty minutes and a nondisclosure agreement with teeth.

d.text: Your brother lifted a drive from a Halcyon sub-basement. On it: every shell company buying Cinder City's paper. Including, fun fact, the Vane apartment building.

e.text: Vivian wants it back quietly. I want to be the one who brings it back quietly. Help me, and your family keeps its roof. That's the whole pitch.

ally.text: Smart. Rare for you. Don't make me regret the compliment, Eli.

refuse.text: Then we're on opposite sides of a very expensive table. I'll wave at you across it.

a.text: The shelter feeds forty and hides one. Guess which number the city cares about.

c.text: A boy who saw your brother pulled into a van and had the sense to run to a church instead of a camera. That sense is why he's still breathing.

d.text: Okoro's sweep will be here by ten. She's honest, which makes her dangerous in a different currency. Decide what the boy is to you: a witness, or a child.

a.text: Vane. I know why you're here and I don't care. Hand me the witness and it's testimony. Hide him and it's obstruction. Those are different bedrooms in the same jail.

law.text: Smart. It'll be on record, signed, and it'll burn somebody with a tall building. I'll take that trade every day of my pension.

spirit.text: Tunnels behind the slag heap. My grandfather dug them for cigarettes; tonight they dig a boy a future. Go.

a.text: Look at it! The family charity case, sweating for pennies! Dad says you're 'disciplined'. Dad says a lot of things about dead people too.

b.text: Your father sent you to watch. That's not trust, Julian. That's a leash.

c.text: ...Enjoy the purse, Vane. Spend it on your brother. Oh wait. Ha. Hm.

a.text: Service lift, floor thirty-one, filing vault behind ARGUS's left eye. You have eight minutes between audit pings.

c.text: Then you meet Halcyon's security staff. They're polite, unionized, and carry batons with serial numbers. Run anyway.

a.text: Anomaly logged: vault mass variance, four grams. Please remain where you are. Compliance is comfort.

b.text: The copy is on your stick, Eli. Leave the original. Originals have fingerprints and funerals.

steal.text: You absolute— fine. FINE. Then we do this the loud way and I hate you slightly more per floor.

copy.text: Good. Quiet. See? We could've been functional together.

a.text: I didn't get kidnapped, Eli. I WENT. I've been in Halcyon's guest cage for nine days trading them silence for your name staying off a list.

c.text: Was Julian improvising! He needed a show to flush the drive out. I played along because if Crowe's son thinks I'm his prisoner, Dad's— YOUR name stays out of the book. That was the whole plan. I'm an idiot, but it was a plan.

a.text: Bulldozers at the Kiln line since dawn. Halcyon paper says 'blight remediation'. My crews say 'our street'.

b.text: You want the haulage trucks at the plaza Friday, you bring me one reason that isn't sentiment. I've got forty men's mortgages and one neck.

a.text: Halcyon buys the docks next, make no mistake. They start with your bricks because bricks don't have a syndicate. Yet.

b.text: I'll stand at the plaza if the price is the berth leases back in my name. Romance dies; leases don't.

a.text: The hearing's a theatre piece and everybody knows their seats. But if someone brings ACTUAL paper— filings, signatures, shells— then my badge stops being decoration.

b.text: Bring paper, Vane. I'll bring the ugly uniform.

a.text: Friday. One room. Every creditor in this city. So we pick which knife to be.

options.label: Burn the ledger, own the dark

expose.text: Paper in daylight. Okoro's badge, Gunnar's trucks, the whole row watching. Halcyon survives scandals; it doesn't survive receipts.

burn.text: Crowe's book is every debt in the underworld, including mine. Ash has no signatures. Whoever holds the matches holds the city.

deal.text: Vivian offers the row stays standing if I hand her the drive and smile for the photo. Everyone eats. Everyone's owned. Everyone's alive.

a.text: Mr. Vane. You've cost me eleven million and one board seat. I find I admire the ratio.

b.text: Sign the transfer and Kiln Row remains residential in perpetuity. A clause I wrote myself, in pencil. Pencil, Mr. Vane. I too have learned your city's idioms.

c.text: Or don't. The plaza is full of witnesses and I have already priced each of them. The pen is the only variable I cannot forecast.

sign.text: Sensible. Welcome to the adult table; the food is fine and the exits are monitored.

tear.text: ...Then we are both about to discover what this city does to people who refuse arithmetic. Do try to bleed on someone else's quarter.

a.text: Noodle Row, ninety seconds, don't lift the lid. The lid is structural. And emotional.
Two patients, two addresses, zero muggings. My malpractice insurer calls this 'optimism'.
Eat first, shop after. That's the house rule and I am the house.
Eyes on the counter, hands where the light is. What'll it be?
Buying, selling, no questions. In that order of enthusiasm.
Cash up front, stories optional. Sit or shop, but stop hovering.
Fresh today! Fresher yesterday! Prices honest both days!
She's got two owners, one dent, and a heart of pure arson. Love her and she'll love you back at 190.
You look like your father when he was about to do something stupid. Sit. Eat. Do it fed.
The docks are calm this week. I made them calm. There's a difference and it's called me.
If you're about to confess something, save it for a day I've had coffee.
I'm clean now. Three weeks clean. Don't say 'proud', say 'buy me dinner'.
Halcyon thinks I'm at a spa. Keep my secret and I'll keep yours; that's what exes are for.
The refinery flare hasn't gone out since 1987. Some nights I preach to it. It's the only congregation that never argues.
Crates don't lie. People do. I schedule accordingly.
Bet you fifty I can idle this thing on two wheels. Don't tell Roz. Actually tell Roz, I need the credibility.
Trigger discipline, sugar. Even in conversation.
You're walking favorably for someone with your chart. Keep it up or keep paying me.
Careful, Vane. My patience is inherited and it's in probate.
Small talk is a loan, Mr. Vane. It accrues.
You're standing in my sightline. That's either courage or unpaid rent.
Confession's free, as always. Though the good ones usually start with 'this will sound worse than it was'.

lines: Don't hang up. You hung up last time and I still think about it.
Halcyon bought your brother's debt, Eli. All of it. Paper and person.
Noir Lounge. One hour. Wear the jacket you pretend not to love.
Berth seven. Tonight's crate is heavier and quieter than last week's.
Same rate. Same rules. Different consequences, probably.
Vane. Your name surfaced in a Crowe audit. Coincidences exist; I've never met one.
Keep your hands boring and your evenings dull. That's the whole call.
